finding.claim: Cache entries for a valid token are only bounded by the token's own exp/nbf when the payload has a numeric `iat`. A signed token that carries `exp` but no `iat` is cached for the full cacheTTL (default 600000 ms) and keeps being accepted after it expires.
finding.source: A validly signed JWT with `exp` set and no numeric `iat`, verified with caching enabled (the `cache` option). Such tokens come from third-party issuers or from this library's signer with `noTimestamp: true`, and then replayed after `exp`. The attacker holds an expired token.
finding.sink: Cache-hit short-circuit in verify() at src/verifier.js:364-378 returns the cached payload without re-running the exp validator.

trace.note: After a successful verifyToken, the result is stored via cacheSet(cacheContext, payload).
hasIat = typeof payload.iat === 'number'; false when iat is absent.
The whole block that reads payload.nbf and payload.exp into cacheValue[1] and cacheValue[2] is nested inside `if (hasIat)` and is skipped.
cacheValue[2] stays 0, so it is set to maxTTL = clockTimestamp + clockTolerance + cacheTTL, which ignores the token's exp.
On later calls the cache lookup runs before decode and validation; the condition `min === 0 && (max === 0 || now <= max)` holds until maxTTL, so the expired token is accepted.

finding.guards_checked: verifyToken's exp validator (src/verifier.js:304-323) is enforced on the first, uncached verification only. The cache hit at line 377 returns before it. maxAge is not applied either, because it needs iat in cacheSet line 126. cacheTTL bounds the window (default 10 min) but does not remove it. `ignoreExpiration` is not set in this scenario. The decoder, signature and algorithm checks all pass, since the token is genuinely signed.
